title: Evaluation and Analysis of Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the frequency of affirmative ('yes') responses from Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to object-based presence queries (e.g., 'Is there a {item} in this photo?') for objects that are absent from the image, in order to reveal the models' tendency to blindly affirm user prompts rather than rely on visual input.

Comparing the evaluation predictions of ChatGPT and HaELM to identify decision-making biases, specifically observing that ChatGPT leans toward predicting the presence of hallucinations, while HaELM leans toward predicting non-hallucination responses.
